text:
**Short answer: 30W is the minimum, and 70W or higher is what you need for fast charging.**

**What Apple recommends** ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)):
- **MacBook Air models from 2022 or later:** 30W (13-inch only), 35W dual-port, 67W, or 70W adapters. These work with the USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable or a regular USB-C cable.
- **2018-2021 models:** a 30W adapter or the 40W Dynamic adapter (60W max) with a USB-C cable.

**What comes in the box:**
- **13-inch M5:** a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ([Apple specs](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **13-inch M4:** a 30W adapter with the 8-core GPU, or a 35W dual-port adapter with the 10-core GPU ([Apple specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).

**Fast charging:** Apple lists the M4 and M5 Airs as fast-charge capable with a 70W or higher USB PD power source. Apple says a 30W adapter is the minimum to charge the M5 Air ([Apple specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/)).

**Any USB-C adapter works.** Apple says any USB Power Delivery adapter will charge a USB-C Mac, even one with higher or lower wattage than recommended. Lower wattage just means slower charging, and for the best experience you should meet the recommended minimum.

**A third-party option:** The [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W charger](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) (2-pack, $49.99 at Baseus's US store as of 2026-10-21) has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A. It's a good fit if you want a second charger for your bag. Some caveats:
- At 65W it's below Apple's 70W fast-charge threshold, so don't expect full fast-charge speeds.
- With multiple devices plugged in, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is still enough for a MacBook Air.
